Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Final validation: VPC/on-prem go-live playbook & smoke tests

Team / Acme,

We’re less than a week out from the scheduled on-prem cutover (Mon 17 Nov). Attached is the compiled go‑live playbook (GoLive_Playbook_v1.2.pdf) and the smoke test checklist (onprem-smoke-checklist.xlsx). Please review for any outstanding items that would block go/no‑go. Key asks:

- Acme: confirm final firewall/port approval and schedule for the maintenance window.
- Security: confirm audit log collection and retention settings in the private control plane.
- Infra: validate capacity test results for sustained 400 RPS baseline.

I’ve also attached a current network diagram (network-diagram.svg). Proposed cutover window: 17 Nov 2025, 01:00–03:00 UTC. If we get a clean signoff by end of day Friday (14 Nov), we’ll proceed. Otherwise we’ll need to postpone by 48 hours.

Attachments: GoLive_Playbook_v1.2.pdf, onprem-smoke-checklist.xlsx, network-diagram.svg

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rohan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Rohan —

Thanks for the bundle. A few quick items from Acme side:

- We need the definitive list of outbound ports the appliance will open (I only saw ranges in the diagram). Can you provide explicit port numbers for procurement and firewall rules?
- Security wants confirmation that audit logs are delivered to our SIEM (Splunk) with no sampling.
- We’ll run a staging cutover on Friday morning (internal) and will provide results by EOD.

I’ve looped in IT Ops and Samantha (platform lead) so they can coordinate the maintenance window. Expect a staging report from us by Friday.

-Michael
Director of Engineering, Acme Corp
Michael.Perez@acmecorp.com

Cc: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Final validation: VPC/on-prem go-live playbook & smoke tests

Michael, team —

Thanks, Michael. I updated the network diagram and appended a definitive port list in the playbook (see page 6). High level:

- Control plane => outbound TCP 443 to *.redwood-api.com (443) for telemetry and control signals.
- Model-serving nodes => outbound TCP 9000–9010 (gRPC) for telemetry, and inbound from load balancer on 8080/8443 for model traffic.
- KV cache sync => UDP 12345 (internal overlay), restricted to the private VPC.

We will deliver a one‑page firewall rule set and a small iptables example for Acme’s edge team before EOD Friday.

Also, notes on audit logs: we push JSON log events over HTTPS to your Splunk ingest endpoint. No sampling; retention policy controlled by Acme’s SIEM.

Attachments: network-diagram.svg (updated)

- Priyom
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Final validation: VPC/on-prem go-live playbook & smoke tests

Quick feedback from running the smoke tests in staging this morning:

- Step 4 (KV cache warmup) timing needs a hard timeout and retry policy in the runbook. I proposed: timeout 180s, 2 retries, then failover to cold-start mode and alert on Slack+PagerDuty.
- Add a verification step for TLS cert chain validation against the on-prem CA (step 2.3).
- Latency thresholds: set post-cutover P95 target to <= 120ms for the base prompt path — we observed 110–130ms in staging; need the runbook to include the rollback trigger (>= 180ms sustained for 5 minutes).

I’ll update the smoke-checklist with these checks and push version 1.1 of the checklist.

Sooj in Lee
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Final validation: VPC/on-prem go-live playbook & smoke tests

Folks —

I ran a capacity validation this afternoon and attached the updated smoke checklist (onprem-smoke-checklist.xlsx). Summary:

- Sustained baseline of 420 RPS for 30m with headroom up to 600 RPS in bursty workloads on the dedicated GPU profile.
- Memory pressure observed under synthetic adversarial prompts; mitigation in playbook step 7.2 (session trimming) is validated.

Action items for Acme: please sign the DocuSign go‑live approval when you receive it. I’ll also upload the detailed logs to the shared folder (see link).

Attachments: onprem-smoke-checklist.xlsx

Diego Fernandez
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com

Michael / Samantha —

Thanks for the quick turn. Based on the staging results and internal validation, Redwood gives a green recommendation for the 17 Nov cutover, provided Acme signs the DocuSign approval and confirms the firewall rules we sent in the playbook. Summary of gating items (must be complete by 14 Nov EOD):

1) DocuSign approval signed by Acme infra lead (Samantha).
2) Firewall rules applied and tested in the staging VLAN.
3) Splunk ingest endpoint confirmed and test event received.
4) Final maintenance window confirmed (we still propose 01:00–03:00 UTC).

If all of the above are confirmed we will:
- Push the on-prem appliance image (v2025.11.1) to your registry at 00:30 UTC on 17 Nov.
- Run the smoke checklist (attached) with SRE on-call live.
- Execute a 30-minute validation bump; rollback plan in playbook section 9.
